description:
**Surfaced 2026-05-16 by user-tier POLYBIUS + PRINCIPAL during ariadne bw 0.13.0 upgrade discussion.** Coupled arc covering BOTH the substrate-level adoption of bw 0.13.0 new features AND the encoding of a bw-upgrade-discipline so future bw releases have a clear process.

The two pieces are coupled deliberately per §15 honest-scope: the discipline is the generalization of the work being done; encoding both together means the discipline gets baked while the empirical anchor is fresh.

## Precondition

ariadne--c71 ships first at ariadne-core (Dockerfile bw 0.12.3 → 0.13.0 + ingest smoke). Local bw is already on 0.13.0. This arc dispatches AFTER c71 has cleanly shipped + user-tier QA passes.

## Part B — adopt bw 0.13.0 features at substrate level

### B.1 — Registry replaces consumer-workspaces.txt (highest leverage)

bw 0.13.0 adds a host-local repository registry: bw registry list/prune + auto-registration when registry.auto is set in global config. This natively does what substrate/consumer-workspaces.txt does manually.

Migration shape:
- substrate/skills/check-substrate-updates/check.sh no-args sweep: replace read of consumer-workspaces.txt with parse of bw registry list output
- Per-workspace filtering: bw registry auto-registration covers Stoa-deployed workspaces naturally
- Deprecate substrate/consumer-workspaces.txt — keep file for one release with a deprecation comment, then remove in a follow-up arc
- Document migration in SKILL.md

Cross-ref: today's stoa--sc8 closure (added the-stoa to consumer-workspaces.txt manually). bw registry obsoletes that manual append.

### B.2 — Cross-repo issue resolution doc (user-tier ergonomic win)

bw 0.13.0: bw show stoa--abc resolves prefix to registered repo without cd-ing. -C accepts registered prefix as well as path. Document this pattern in MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §7 (Communication / bw operations) and operating-disciplines.md §12 (bw cookbook) as the canonical navigation pattern for user-tier POLYBIUS working across workspaces.

### B.3 — Attachments as available primitive

bw 0.13.0: bw attach ticket-id file-path stores arbitrary files under attachments/ticket-id/path on the beadwork ref. Document in MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §16 (POLYBIUS lifecycle / multi-artifact handoff) as an available primitive: handoff doc, retro, design artifact can optionally be attached to their parent ticket rather than only on disk. Forward-only convention; don't migrate existing on-disk artifacts.

### B.4 — Recap as available primitive

bw 0.13.0: bw recap shows cursor-driven incremental activity across registered repos. Document in MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §16 (POLYBIUS lifecycle) and/or §7 (Communication) as an available primitive for cross-session continuity — POLYBIUS picking up after compaction can run bw recap to see what has happened since its last read-point. Forward-only convention.

## Part C — bw-upgrade discipline (the generalization)

### C.1 — operating-disciplines.md new section: bw-upgrade discipline

Encode the process for handling future bw releases:

1. **Trigger:** new bw release tagged upstream (manual check OR via C.2 skill).
2. **Review:** read changelog; classify features by impact axis:
   - **Deployment-side:** Railway container Dockerfile bump; consumer-install scripts; SHA256 update.
   - **Substrate-side:** does this obsolete substrate canon? does it enable new substrate patterns? (e.g., 0.13.0 registry obsoleted consumer-workspaces.txt per B.1)
   - **Workspace-side:** UX changes; new commands; output format / exit code changes (the bw_ingest.py-style subprocess-regression risk).
3. **File tickets:** one per impact axis with concrete action.
4. **Dispatch:** standard arcs per workspace.
5. **Verification:** existing substrate consumers still work; subprocess-call sites in any code (e.g., bw_ingest.py) verified under new version.

### C.2 — Lightweight skill: substrate/skills/check-bw-release/

Mirror the shape of check-substrate-updates. On-demand or cron-driven:

1. Query the bw GitHub releases API for current latest tag
2. Compare to a known-baseline (stored in a small state file, similar to .substrate-last-check)
3. If new release detected: print changelog excerpt + impact-axis classification template (per C.1) + suggested next action
4. Operator can cron the check or run on-demand

The skill operationalizes step 1 of the discipline; classification + filing is still operator (POLYBIUS) judgment.

## Empirical anchor for the discipline

The 0.12.3 → 0.13.0 work being done now IS the discipline first worked example. ariadne--c71 demonstrates the deployment-side axis (Dockerfile bump + ingest smoke). B.1-B.4 demonstrate the substrate-side axis (canon adoption). Cross-ref both as the worked-example pointer in operating-disciplines.md §C.1.

## Deliverables (sketch — DAEDALUS scopes precisely)

1. substrate/skills/check-substrate-updates/check.sh — replace consumer-workspaces.txt read with bw registry list parse (B.1)
2. substrate/consumer-workspaces.txt — add deprecation comment; mark for removal in follow-up arc (B.1)
3. substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §7 OR §12 — document cross-repo resolution pattern (B.2)
4. substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §16 — document attachments + recap as available primitives (B.3, B.4)
5. substrate/operating-disciplines.md — new section: bw-upgrade discipline with 5-step process + impact-axis classification (C.1)
6. substrate/skills/check-bw-release/SKILL.md + check.sh — lightweight release-check skill (C.2)
7. substrate/install.sh — SKILL_NAMES append for new skill (mirror Arc 25 credential-discipline + Arc 26 check-substrate-updates patterns)

## Acceptance (probes — VERA scopes precisely)

- check.sh no-args sweep against current registered workspaces returns same set as today consumer-workspaces.txt list (regression check)
- bw registry list output is parseable by the substituted check.sh logic
- bw show stoa--abc from arbitrary working directory resolves correctly per B.2 doc
- check-bw-release skill executes against current bw release and reports current if at 0.13.0; reports new release detected if a future tag is mocked in
- operating-disciplines.md bw-upgrade-discipline section reads coherently with the rest of the doc
- Authorship: all new files credit Denson Smith; no LLM-placeholder author fields

## Out of scope (hard-locked)

- ariadne--c71 (separate arc; ships first; this arc waits)
- Removing consumer-workspaces.txt entirely (one-release deprecation; removal is follow-up arc)
- Adopting bw 0.13.0 features beyond B.1-B.4 (any future-bw-release follow-on adoption is its own ticket)
- Migrating existing on-disk handoff/retro/design artifacts to attachments (forward-only; existing artifacts stay where they are)
- check-bw-release skill cron-scheduling defaults (skill exists; operator decides whether to cron)
- Cross-workspace propagation of new skill (substrate update arc deploys it via install.sh; consumer workspaces get it on next apply)

## §15 N=1 caveat

The bw-upgrade discipline (C) is encoded with N=1 empirical anchor (this 0.12.3 → 0.13.0 work). PRINCIPAL declared the need for a discipline today (project-direction authority); substrate canon enters off-gate. Future bw releases accrete supporting evidence per §6.7.1 three-condition gate; if the discipline classification axes turn out wrong-shaped, future arcs revise.
